A '''[[Rakata/Legends|Rakatan]] prisoner''' lived during the [[Infinite Empire/Legends|Infinite Empire's]] dominance over [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. His quest for personal power resulted in his own kind imprisoning his consciousness in a [[mind prison]]. His consciousness vessel was eventually rediscovered during the [[Jedi Civil War]].

==Biography==
The Rakata individual lived sometime during the height of the Infinite Empire. For his crimes his conscousness was extracted from his physical body to be placed in a [[Unidentified Rakatan prisoner's mind prison|mechanical vessel]], one of many [[mind prison]]s used in the [[Infinite Empire/Legends|Infinite Empire]].<ref name="KOTOR" />

With the eventual fall of the Rakata, he lay dormant and forgotten in his prison for thousands of years. Eventually his mind prison was re-discovered and got into hands of [[Revan/Legends|Revan]], who unwillingly briefly entered the prison, and encountered its Rakatan inhabitant during his [[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic|second search for the Star Forge]].<ref name="KOTOR" />

The imprisoned Rakatan knew how to perform a ritual that could release another from the Rakatan Prison. He made a deal with Revan, the most recent to enter the endless void. If Revan could defeat him in a game of riddles, he would be free. However, if Revan lost, the prisoner would get out and inhabit Revan's body, dooming him to an eternity in the box. After a few riddles, Revan stumped him. The prisoner stayed inside and reluctantly released Revan, helping the hero along with his quest for the [[Star Forge]].<ref name="KOTOR" />

==Behind the scenes==
An unidentified Rakatan prisoner appeared in the ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]'' video game. The riddle game he plays with Revan seems to be inspired by chapter five of [[Wikipedia:J.R.R. Tolkien|J.R.R. Tolkien]]'s [[Wikipedia:The Hobbit|''The Hobbit'']]: "Riddles In The Dark". In this chapter, [[Wikipedia:Bilbo Baggins|Bilbo Baggins]], the titular [[Wikipedia:Hobbit|Hobbit]], engages in a Riddle-game with a being called [[Wikipedia:Gollum|Gollum]] in order to avoid being eaten.<ref name="Hobbit">{{BookCite|author=[[Wikipedia:J.R.R. Tolkien|Tolkien, J.R.R.]]|container=Chapter V: Riddles In The Dark|title=[[Wikipedia:The Hobbit|The Hobbit]]|publisher=[[Wikipedia:George Allen & Unwin|George Allen & Unwin]]|date=1937}}</ref> Indeed, one of the riddles used by the Rakatan was first used in ''The Hobbit'' by Gollum. This riddle was, "What has roots as nobody sees, is taller than trees, up, up it goes, and yet never grows?"<ref name="KOTOR" />
